ai.title: Increase OpenRouter timeout for deep-thinking models
ai.summary: Extended headers timeout to 10 minutes in web/src/llm-api/openrouter.ts to handle delayed streaming starts for models like gpt-5. Uses undici Agent with headersTimeout set to 600000ms and bodyTimeout disabled. Applied via custom dispatcher in createOpenRouterRequest.

eli5.text: When the system talks to certain advanced AI models (like GPT-5) through OpenRouter, those models can take several minutes before they start sending a response. To keep those conversations from failing, the software now waits up to 10 minutes for the model to begin streaming its answer instead of giving up after a shorter period. If you use a deep-thinking model through OpenRouter, you’ll notice the system no longer times out while the model is still thinking and preparing its reply. No action is needed on your part; the extended wait now applies automatically whenever an OpenRouter request is made.

ai.title: CLI 1.0.610 ships referral bonus grant and Stripe checkout invoice
ai.summary: CLI version 1.0.610 packages referral bonuses, Stripe invoice creation, OpenRouter timeout extensions, terminal width rendering, and the subscription limit banner with /subscribe command. Referral rewards converted from monthly recurring 250 credits to one-time 500-credit grants that never expire, with legacy referrals migrated via a manual backfill script. Stripe checkout sessions now create invoices and collect tax IDs for both credit purchases and subscriptions, while OpenRouter requests use a 10-minute headersTimeout to accommodate delayed streaming starts from deep-thinking models like gpt-5. Terminal command previews render at full available width via the new availableWidth prop, and the CLI now shows a dynamic WEBSITE_URL in the usage banner instead of a hardcoded domain.
ai.evidence: The diff shows a single version bump in `cli/release/package.json` from `1.0.609` to `1.0.610`, with no other modified files. Release instructions indicate this row aggregates all user-visible changes since 1.0.609, listed as updates through 2026-02-05.

eli5.text: This release improves the Codebuff experience by giving referral rewards as a one-time bonus of 500 credits (up from 250 monthly), adding a new in-app subscription limit banner with a /subscribe command, enabling Stripe checkout to create invoices and collect tax IDs, and making terminal command previews use the full terminal width. Referral bonuses now never expire and older recurring referrals are handled separately. The CLI usage banner now dynamically shows the correct website URL instead of a hardcoded domain. These changes mean you get more flexible credit rewards, clearer guidance when you hit usage limits, cleaner invoices for purchases, and better use of your terminal space when previewing commands.

ai.summary: The CLI package was bumped to 1.0.611, packaging three user-facing improvements that landed since 1.0.610. The subscription API now accepts bearer token authentication via `extractApiKeyFromHeader` with NextAuth session fallback, and a new `getUserIdFromSessionToken` helper resolves the userId from session tokens with expiry checks. eli5.text: This release makes logging in more secure and keeps you from accidentally closing your session while you're hitting your monthly usage limits. You can now authenticate using a bearer token when accessing your subscription details, which improves how web apps verify identity without breaking the browser-based sign-in flow. When you reach your spend limit, the chat input bar stays hidden so you only see the limit message, preventing accidental typing into a locked session. Additionally, pressing Escape or Backspace no longer lets you exit this restricted mode, ensuring you acknowledge the limit before continuing. These changes together make rate-limit messaging clearer and protect your session from premature closure during billing cutoffs.

ai.title: Add BuffBench remote trigger script and CI workflow
ai.summary: Added `trigger-buffbench.ts` script and `.github/workflows/buffbench.yml` to enable remote execution of the BuffBench eval suite. The workflow uses `workflow_dispatch` with a 360-minute timeout, setting up Bun 1.3.5 and injecting secrets via `generate-ci-env.ts`. The `evals/buffbench/main.ts` configuration was updated to run only the `base2` agent with `taskConcurrency` increased to 5. This change introduces a new `trigger-buffbench` npm script in `evals/package.json` for local invocation.

eli5.text: You can now kick off the BuffBench evaluation suite remotely from a local terminal instead of only through the automated system that already ran it. A new command lets developers start the same test run manually, pointing it at whatever branch they are currently on, and the results are still delivered privately to CodebuffAI members who already had access. The suite itself now runs only the core test agent, but tests five of them at the same time instead of one at a time, so each manual run finishes faster. The new triggering tool is ready to use today.

ai.title: Simplify CLI credit spending toggle semantics
ai.summary: Refactors `subscription-limit-banner.tsx` and `usage-banner.tsx` to replace the complex "always use credits" checkbox and "switch to spend/pause" button with a direct `Credit spending: enabled/disabled` toggle. This change aligns the UI state with backend semantics by treating the `fallbackToALaCarte` flag as a simple boolean for credit spending enablement rather than a conditional fallback mechanism. The `usage-banner` now displays explicit status text and a single action button, while `subscription-limit-banner` conditionally renders credit continuation options only when spending is enabled.

eli5.text: If you use the command-line assistant and hit your monthly usage limit, you'll now see a clear switch labeled "Credit spending: enabled" or "Credit spending: disabled" instead of the old checkbox and multi-button setup. Toggling that switch directly controls whether your paid credits get used after your subscription runs out, matching how the system actually tracks that setting behind the scenes. The status line and available actions update instantly to show either that your credits will keep working or that you've paused that automatic spending. This is live today for anyone who sees those usage banners in their terminal.

Upgrading gives you faster, clearer control over both evaluation runs and billing preferences.
